_note: Reviewed safety-first guidance for members of the public. The AI only CHOOSES a card; it never writes medical advice. Every card starts with personal safety and ends with when to get professional help.

_sources.PFA: People For Animals India, Emergency first aid: https://www.peopleforanimalsindia.org/public/first-aid
_sources.HW: Humane World for Animals, How to safely help a stray: https://www.humaneworld.org/en/resources/how-safely-help-stray-pet
_sources.BC: Blue Cross (UK), Basic first aid for dogs: https://www.bluecross.org.uk/1958-2781/basic-first-aid.html
_sources.WHO: World Health Organization, Rabies fact sheet: https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/rabies

road_injury.title: Hurt by a vehicle
steps: Keep yourself safe first. Don't step into moving traffic.
Don't touch or lift the animal. A scared, hurt animal can bite.
Stand where drivers can see you and wave them to slow down.
Keep people and other animals back so it stays calm.
If a helper asks you to, a cloth or cardboard can be placed nearby for shade. Don't force water or food.

bleeding.title: Bleeding
steps: Don't touch the animal with bare hands. A hurt animal can bite.
Keep it calm and still. Stay back and keep the area quiet.
Only a trained helper should press a clean cloth on the wound.
Don't put turmeric, oil or powders on the wound.

trapped.title: Trapped or stuck
steps: Don't pull the animal out yourself. You can hurt it, or get bitten.
Note exactly where it is stuck and how (drain, wire, gate, well).
Keep a crowd from gathering. Noise makes it panic.
Wait for a helper with gloves and tools.

aggressive_or_scared.title: Scared or aggressive animal
steps: Keep a safe distance. Don't stare, shout or run.
Don't try to catch or feed it by hand.
Keep children and other animals away.
Helpers with experience will handle it.

heat_stress.title: Weak in the heat
steps: Don't touch it if it seems scared or hurt.
If it is calm, place a bowl of clean water near it. Don't pour water into its mouth.
Give shade with cloth or cardboard if you can do it safely.

cattle_on_road.title: Cattle on the road
steps: Never try to push or chase cattle on a busy road. They can kick or run into traffic.
Warn drivers: stand safely at the side and signal them to slow down.
At night, a phone torch helps drivers see you, not the animal.
Wait for the helper or municipal team to move it safely.

sick.title: Looks sick
steps: Don't touch it with bare hands.
Note what you see: vomiting, not walking, wounds, eye or skin problems.
Keep a small bowl of clean water nearby if it's calm.
Don't give human medicines like paracetamol. They can be poisonous to animals.

dead_animal.title: Animal has died
steps: Thank you for caring. Please don't touch it.
If it's on the road, warn drivers from a safe place.
StrayWatch will share how to reach the municipal team for removal.

puppies_or_kittens.title: Babies on their own
steps: Don't pick them up straight away. The mother may be close by.
Watch from a distance for a while.
If they're in danger (road, rain, drain), a helper will move them to a safe spot nearby.

general.title: Stay safe while you help
steps: Keep a safe distance and stay calm.
Don't touch, lift or feed the animal by hand.
Keep people and traffic away from it.

bite_rule: If anyone is bitten or scratched: wash the wound with soap and running water for 15 minutes, and go to a hospital for a rabies vaccine today. Rabies is almost always fatal once symptoms start, and fully preventable with prompt vaccination.
